title: Energy Transfer in Ecosystems
seo_title: JSS 1 Intermediate Science: Energy Transfer in Ecosystems Worksheets (NERDC)
standard_code: JSS 1 Intermediate Science: Learning About Our Environment
standard_text: Energy flows through ecosystems from producers to consumers along food chains and food webs; only about 10% of the energy passes to the next trophic level; ecological pyramids show energy, numbers and biomass. (summary of the Intermediate Science curriculum, JSS 1, theme: Learning About Our Environment)
meta_desc: Free JSS 1 Intermediate Science worksheets (NERDC curriculum, theme: Learning About Our Environment): food chains and webs, trophic levels, the 10% rule, ecological pyramids and decomposers. 100 questions with answers.
key_sub: About 10% of energy passes to the next trophic level.
body_html:
How to think about it

Producers (plants and algae) capture energy from sunlight by photosynthesis. Herbivores are primary consumers; carnivores are secondary and tertiary consumers; decomposers break down dead matter. Each feeding level is a trophic level.

At each level most energy is used for life processes or lost as heat, so only about 10% passes on. This is why food chains are short and top predators are few. Ecological pyramids of energy, numbers and biomass show this pattern.

Example

Producers have 10,000 kJ. About how much reaches primary consumers?

10%

Answer: 1,000 kJ

Example

Which organisms return nutrients to the soil?

Bacteria and fungi

Answer: decomposers

Common mistakes

  • Thinking energy is recycled in an ecosystem.
  • Drawing food chain arrows the wrong way (arrows show where energy goes).
  • Leaving decomposers out of a food web.

faq.q: Why are there more rice plants than rice birds in a field?
faq.a: Energy decreases at each level, so higher levels support fewer organisms.

faq.q: Why do arrows point from the plant to the animal?
faq.a: They show the direction energy flows.

items.q: Food chain: grass → grasshoppers → mice → snakes. What trophic level are the mice?
items.e: Count from the producer.

items.q: Food chain: phytoplankton → zooplankton → small fish → tuna. What trophic level are the tuna?

items.q: Food chain: phytoplankton → zooplankton → small fish → tuna. What trophic level are the zooplankton?

items.q: Tobi's energy pyramid shows 2,000 units of energy in the producers. About 10% passes to each level above. About how much energy reaches the secondary consumers?
items.e: Divide by 10 for each level: 2,000 → 200 → 20.

items.q: The algae capture 50,000 kJ of energy. Using the 10% rule, about how much reaches the snails?
items.e: Divide by 10 for each step: 1 step.

items.q: The grass capture 100,000 kJ of energy. Using the 10% rule, about how much reaches the mice?
items.e: Divide by 10 for each step: 2 steps.

items.e: Less energy supports fewer animals.

items.q: Producers in a food chain fix 50,000 J of energy. Using the 10% law, how much energy reaches the secondary consumers?
items.e: Only about 10% passes to each level: 50,000 × 0.12 = 500 J.

items.q: Producers in a food chain fix 600,000 J of energy. Using the 10% law, how much energy reaches the secondary consumers?
items.e: Only about 10% passes to each level: 600,000 × 0.12 = 6,000 J.

items.q: A single eucalyptus supports thousands of caterpillars. What shape is the pyramid of numbers?
c: inverted at the base (one producer, many consumers)
items.e: Pyramids of numbers can be inverted; pyramids of energy cannot.

items.q: The primary consumers contain 8,000 kJ m⁻² year⁻¹ and the secondary consumers contain 640 kJ m⁻² year⁻¹. Calculate the efficiency of energy transfer.
items.e: Efficiency = energy at next level ÷ energy at previous level × 100 = 8.00%.

items.q: In a food web, what happens to the number of crickets if most of the frogs that eat them are removed?
items.e: Less predation lets the prey population grow.

items.q: Producers in a food chain fix 50,000 J of energy. Using the 10% law, how much energy reaches the tertiary consumers?
items.e: Only about 10% passes to each level: 50,000 × 0.13 = 50.0 J.

items.q: What is the role of producers?
c: releasing all their energy as heat
converting light energy into chemical energy in organic molecules
items.e: Producers fix energy by photosynthesis.

items.q: Tertiary consumers in a food chain receive 70 J. Using the 10% law, how much energy did the producers fix?
items.e: Go back three levels: 70 × 10³ = 70,000 J.

items.q: Why do food chains rarely have more than four or five links?
c: plants cannot support more than one consumer
there is too much biomass at the top
too little energy is left at the top to support another level
items.e: Energy decreases at each trophic level.

items.q: What is a trophic level?
c: a feeding position in a food chain
the number of organisms in a habitat
items.e: Producers are level 1, herbivores level 2.

items.q: Why is energy lost between trophic levels?
c: much is used in respiration and released as heat, and some is in undigested waste
energy is destroyed at each level
all the energy is stored as biomass
items.e: Typically only about 10% passes to the next level.

items.q: What does a pyramid of biomass show?
c: the dry mass of organisms at each trophic level
the number of organisms at each level
items.e: Biomass is measured per unit area.

items.q: Which pyramid can never be inverted?
items.e: Energy always decreases up the levels.

items.q: Which statement about matter and energy in ecosystems is correct?
c: energy is recycled, but matter is lost
matter is recycled, but energy flows through and is lost as heat
items.e: Energy enters as sunlight and leaves as heat.

items.q: A woodland has a net primary production of 10,800 kJ m⁻² year⁻¹ and respiratory losses of 7,200 kJ m⁻² year⁻¹. Calculate the gross primary production.
items.e: GPP = NPP + R = 18,000 kJ m⁻² year⁻¹.

items.q: Why is phosphate needed by plants?
c: to make ATP, DNA and phospholipids
items.e: Phosphate comes from rocks, not the air.

items.q: A crop has a gross primary production of 30,000 kJ m⁻² year⁻¹ and loses 19,500 kJ m⁻² year⁻¹ in respiration. Calculate its net primary production.

items.q: Why is the pyramid of energy always upright?
c: energy is lost at each step, so less is available at higher levels
items.e: About 10% passes on.

items.q: What is net production in a consumer?
c: chemical energy in food minus energy lost in faeces, urine and respiration
items.e: N = I − (F + R).

items.q: A crop has a gross primary production of 12,000 kJ m⁻² year⁻¹ and loses 6,000 kJ m⁻² year⁻¹ in respiration. Calculate its net primary production.

items.q: What is nitrification?

bacteria oxidise ammonium to nitrites and then nitrates
nitrogen gas is converted to ammonia

items.q: Use the pond food web. The energy in the dragonfly's food first came from

items.q: In the food chain grass → rabbit → hawk, which organism gets the least energy from the sun?
items.e: Energy is lost at each step, so the last organism in the chain gets the least.

items.q: What is a top predator?

items.e: Such as an owl or a fox.

items.q: In this sea food web, what is the role of the zooplankton?

items.e: Look at what it eats in the web.
